entities.summary: The pronunciation of GIF, an acronym for the Graphics Interchange Format, has been disputed since the 1990s. Popularly rendered in English as a one-syllable word, the acronym is most commonly pronounced GHIF or JIF, differing in the phoneme represented by the letter G. Many public figures and institutions have taken sides in the debate; Steve Wilhite, the computer scientist who created the Graphics Interchange Format, gave a speech at the 2013 Webby Awards arguing for the soft-g pronunciation. Others have pointed to the term's origin from abbreviation of the hard-g word graphics to argue for the other pronunciation.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The pronunciation of GIF has had a limited but notable impact on internet culture and language, with significant debate among public figures and institutions since the 1990s. While it may seem trivial, the dispute highlights the complexities of language evolution and the power of online communities to shape linguistic norms.
